questions.question: Day 17 Practice (Weekend Plans & Weather (Phase 2)): When talking about tidying up the room (right now), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'The store vendor'?

options.a: I am tidy up room.
options.b: I was tidying up the room right now.
options.c: He is tidy up room.
options.d: I am tidying up the room right now.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "I am tidying up the room right now.".

questions.question: Day 17 Vocabulary (Weekend Plans & Weather (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'drop by'?

options.a: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.b: Visit someone informally for a short time.
options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'drop by' means: visit someone informally for a short time. Example: "Feel free to drop by our home this evening."

questions.question: Day 17 Vocabulary (Weekend Plans & Weather (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'run errands'?

options.a: Do short daily trips for chores.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'run errands' means: do short daily trips for chores. Example: "I need to run errands at the market before dinner."

questions.question: Day 17 Vocabulary (Weekend Plans & Weather (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'hedge against'?

questions.question:
Day 17 Translation Scenario 1 (Weekend Plans & Weather (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ముందుగా సమస్య యొక్క మూలకారణాన్ని కనుగొనాలి."
(Literal attempt: "First problem root cause finding wanted.")

options.a: I am needing to first problem root cause finding wanted.
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: First problem root cause finding wanted.
options.d: First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue."

Use 'First and foremost' and 'identify the root cause'.

questions.question:

Telugu: "నాకు కొంచెం తలనొప్పిగా ఉంది, ఒక గంట సేపు రెస్ట్ తీసుకుంటాను."
(Literal attempt: "To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.")

options.a: I am needing to to me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.b: I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour.
options.c: To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour."

Say 'I have a slight headache' instead of literal translations.

questions.question:
Day 17 Translation Scenario 3 (Weekend Plans & Weather (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Literal attempt: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.
options.c: I am needing to these tomatoes kg how much? pick give fresh.
options.d: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me."

Use 'per kilo' for price and 'pick out' for selection.
